03 / THE IMPLEMENTATION / CONTINUUM / VERA

A persistent environment for a durable principal.

Continuum is Asentxia’s flagship machine-native runtime substrate and reference implementation of DCA. Its center is VERA — Verifiable Entity with Revocable Authority.

THE PRINCIPAL IS NOT THE PROCESS

The principal is not the process

A VERA retains conceptual identity while models, prompts, sessions, processes, credentials, runtimes, or hosts may change around it. This is the architecture’s principal model, not a claim that all such substitutions are currently verified.

Identity and responsibility remain distinct from replaceable implementation components.

CONTINUUM COMPUTER

Continuum Computer

A persistent logical computing resource distinct from any one VM, host, process, model, or session. The bounded current test preserved the same Continuum Computer ID and VERA ID across distinct OS processes on the same host.

Inspect the bounded claim ↗

WHAT THE LAUNCH SLICE COVERS

What the launch slice covers

The documented same-host process-restart slice includes durable-state recovery, an active scoped grant permitting a capability, revocation denying it, a mediated effect after restart, ordered structured evidence, and an independent verifier.

The scope is same-host process restart. Public artifact links for the exact demo and P00–P01–P03 records are pending.

GOVERNANCE AROUND THE RUNTIME

Governance around the runtime

The Regency is the governance and organizational product for VERAs and multi-VERA structures. Regency Core provides bounded-authority and organizational-validation mechanisms; Regency Console is the authorized human administration and supervision client.

This describes product placement. It does not assert a completed end-to-end integration.

THE GOVERNING PRINCIPLE

The principal persists. The components may change.
